definition.title: Supersymmetry breaking transmitted to light sectors
definition.question: How do heavy non-supersymmetric matter and hidden-sector supersymmetry breaking affect the structure and light scalar dynamics of a gravitational effective theory?
definition.summary: Keeps preservation of a light gravity sector's potential structure distinct from the induced-mass problem for quintessence.

systems: Light approximately supersymmetric gravity coupled to heavy Standard Model matter
targets: Consistency of matter coupling and low-energy scalar-potential structure
regimes: A separated canonical F-term test model
assumptions: Additive separation of K and W does not establish gravitational decoupling
conventions: The canonical example is not a theorem about every possible Kähler geometry
includes: The hierarchy between an induced gravitino-scale mass and the late-time evolution scale
excludes: An established equivalence between the two transmission mechanisms

definition.readingLimit: The canonical quintessence example has bounded primary support. The heavy-Standard-Model question is description-only; protection mechanisms and general radiative stability are not checked.

qualifications: This inventory follows exact factor references. It does not assert that every listed scoped question relies on the withdrawn premise; intact source-target agreement may survive a separate substantive inspection. No factor premise is promoted through all same-paper units.
